title: The spectrum of acute bacterial meningitis in elderly patients (Domingo et al., BMC Infect Dis. 2013;13:108)

claims.text: Meningococcal meningitis is less frequent in elderly patients (>=65 years) than in younger adults.
claims.byte_quote: Meningococcal meningitis was less frequent in elderly patients (P < 0.0001)

claims.text: Listerial meningitis (Listeria monocytogenes) is more frequent in elderly patients.
claims.byte_quote: whereas listerial (P = 0.0196), gram-negative bacillary (P = 0.0065), and meningitis of unknown origin (P = 0.0076) were more frequent

claims.text: Gram-negative bacillary meningitis is more frequent in elderly patients.

claims.byte_quote: and meningitis of unknown origin (P = 0.0076) were more frequent

claims.text: Bacterial meningitis in the elderly tends to have a non-meningococcal etiology.

claims.text: Advanced age (>=65 years) raises the risk of acute bacterial meningitis: incidence 7.40/100,000/year in the elderly vs 4.03/100,000 in adults 15-64 (RR 1.84).
claims.byte_quote: The incidence was 4.03/100,000 (Group I) and 7.40 /100,000 inhabitants/year (Group II) (RR = 1.84; 95%CI: 1.56-2.17, P < 0.0001)
